research.question: Does 18–19 Nov reporting show whether the draft joint statement still 'welcomes the conclusion of negotiations' on the Youth Experience Scheme or has been downgraded to a commitment to conclude later, and is the cap settled?
research.finding: No 19 Nov report settles the wording or the cap. The Guardian (17 Nov 17:50Z) quotes the draft: 'aim to apply this agreement no later than 2028 ... opportunities ... no later than January 2030' – an application date, consistent with 'welcomes the conclusion'; quota expected about 100,000. National Pulse (18 Nov): cap 'still being negotiated'. No reported Coreper outcome. Not decisive; spread kept.

disagreement.note: Blind estimates spanned 0.40–0.88 because the forecasters had different readings of the 17 Nov draft: the dossier (the i, Euronews: 'yet to agree', 'seal by 2028') against Agence Europe's verbatim quote ('welcomes the conclusion of negotiations') found by the evidence forecaster. All five were given the union of facts (no numbers) and gave final estimates 0.62–0.85; the anchor's first number is kept in rounds. Final spread 0.23 (below the 0.25 limit, above 0.15, so research was run; not decisive). The evidence forecaster's stated p_held 0.70 contradicts its own p and the slip rate and is not recorded. decomposition.note: The new facts concern the outcome, not timing: the summit is still set for 20 Nov (slip rate 0.008). The re-reading of the 17 Nov draft (Agence Europe's verbatim 'welcomes the conclusion of negotiations'; '2028' is the application date) and the UK factsheet ('will be agreed') raise p_if_held; the 19 Nov reports (Irish Times: set to ink a deal creating the programme; Daily Mail: cap still contested) leave it there. Afternoon p_held is the geometric mean of base-rate and adversarial; p_if_held is scaled to the published figure.

red_team.case_for_morning: Two outlets (the i, Euronews) read the 17 Nov draft as 'yet to agree' with sealing 'by 2028'. Agence Europe shows the cap and the 2028 date still bracketed, and Coreper was still redrafting on 18 Nov. The Daily Mail (19 Nov) says 'frantic negotiations' continue and the cap is 'a central point of contention'. The EU could hold the scheme back as leverage on tuition fees, and the Guardian flagged a slip to May 2027. A text that only commits to agree the terms later resolves NO.
red_team.case_for_larger: The 17 Nov draft itself, quoted verbatim by Agence Europe, still 'welcomes the conclusion of negotiations on a Youth Experience Scheme' – YES wording; 2028 is an application date, so the morning dossier misread it. The UK government's own factsheet (updated 18 Nov) says the scheme 'will be agreed at the UK-EU Summit on 20 November'. The criterion accepts 'agreed in principle' and 'with or without a cap'. Summit slip about 0.8%. That points to 0.85–0.9.
red_team.verdict: The case for going higher is stronger: the morning figure rested on a misreading of the draft, and official UK text plus the verbatim draft back the YES reading. The leftover risk – the cap or fees fight producing wording that defers agreement – is real but small. Both post-freeze facts bear on p_if_held, not timing. Publish 82%, the calibrated figure.
